claims.text: FairSEP constructs a sensitive subspace from per-class centroid differences between sensitive groups.
FairSEP debiases embeddings by removing their sensitive subspace projections.
FairSEP enforces prediction consistency between original and debiased representations.
FairSEP utilizes a conditional Wasserstein loss to minimize the Wasserstein distance between predictive distributions of sensitive groups conditioned on true labels.
FairSEP employs a Pareto-based optimization strategy that automatically adjusts loss weights to resolve trade-offs among objectives.

methodologies.name: FairSEP
methodologies.description: A Pareto-optimized framework for group fairness in graph neural networks that integrates sensitive subspace projection debiasing, prediction consistency, and conditional Wasserstein loss.

limitations.text: Predictive Equality (ΔFPR) remains under-explored in existing group fairness GNN methods, potentially leading to disparate error risks.
Existing fairness methods rely on a single surrogate loss, which is insufficient to achieve multiple fairness criteria simultaneously.
Existing methods apply uniform debiasing across different label groups, making it difficult to separately address group disparities in positive and negative classes.
